name: Gishpa
title: Overseer of the temple servants
summary: Gishpa was one of those who had oversight over the temple servants (the Nethinim) in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile. He is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as a leader among the temple servants who lived on the Ophel hill in Jerusalem. His role was to organize and supervise those who served at the temple.

keyEvents.title: Overseer of the temple servants
keyEvents.description: Gishpa is mentioned as one of the overseers of the temple servants (the Nethinim) who lived on the Ophel hill in Jerusalem after the exile.

keyEvents.title: Settlement of the temple servants on Ophel
keyEvents.description: The temple servants, under the leadership of Shiha and Gishpa, settled on the Ophel hill near the temple to carry out their service.

keyEvents.title: Rebuilding of Jerusalem's community
keyEvents.description: As part of Nehemiah's reorganization of Jerusalem, leaders were appointed for various groups, including the temple servants for whom Gishpa was responsible.

keyEvents.title: Registration of the inhabitants of Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: Gishpa is mentioned in connection with the great registration of those who lived in Jerusalem, which was part of Nehemiah's plan to repopulate the rebuilt city.
